      <title>Norsk målfest i NHL – Solberg og Zuccarello med scoringer</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/norsk-malfest-i-nhl-_-solberg-og-zuccarello-med-scoringer-1.18090062</link>
      <description>Stian Solberg leverte sin første fulltreffer i NHL da han satte kampens første i oppgjøret mellom Anaheim Ducks og Los Angeles Kings. Like etterpå kom nummer to.
Begge kom i førsteperioden mot Mats Zuccarellos lag.
1-0 satt i nettet med fem minutter igjen av de første 20. Solberg fikk pucken rett foran mål og beholdt roen før han banket inn kampens første.
– Han er 20 år, men han har vist så stor ro etter at han fikk sjansen i NHL. Dette er et eksempel på det. Se hvordan han holder på pucken, han kjenner ikke presset, sa kommentatoren på Viaplays sending.
Like etterpå prøvde Solberg seg igjen, og fra avstand lurte han inn nummer to.
I andreperioden viste Zuccarello sin klassse da han styrte inn 1-2.
Dagen etter thanksgiving kunne hockeyinteresserte amerikanere benke seg for å følge hele 15 NHL-kamper.
I tre av dem var det norske spillere på banen, og en av dem var et ekte norsk oppgjør.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>For å prøve å løse budsjettfloken på Stortinget er det kontakt mellom de parlamentariske lederne i Ap, MDG, SV, Rødt og Senterpartiet, etter det NRK erfarer.
Det er også planlagt direkte samtaler mellom Arbeiderpartiets Tonje Brenna og MDGs Ingrid Liland i dag.
Kilder i partiene sier lite tyder på en snarlig løsning, som kan få MDG om bord.
For Ap, SV, Sp og Rødt framstår det som uklart hva MDG forlanger av konkrete gjennomslag for å kunne stemme for statsbudsjettet.
De fire partiene har på sin side så langt avvist å endre budsjettavtalen som ble inngått onsdag.
Finanskomiteen på Stortinget skal avgi sin innstilling om statsbudsjett på mandag. Selve voteringen i stortingssalen skjer 7. desember.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/mann-tok-seg-inn-i-boligen-til-hoiby-_-na-er-saken-henlagt-1.18089585</link>
      <description>Politiet har etterforsket saken der en mann tok seg inn til Marius Borg Høiby på Skaugum og har besluttet å henlegge saken etter bevisets stilling.
Det opplyser Oslo politidistrikt i en pressemelding fredag.
– Påtalemyndigheten har kommet til at det etter etterforskningen er rimelig tvil om siktedes skyldevne på tidspunktet for den anmeldte hendelsen, skriver politiet.
Mannen har ikke ønsket å forklare seg for politiet, men det er gjennomført avhør av fornærmede og vitneavhør. Han har selv nektet for å ha gjort noe straffbart.
I tillegg er det gjennomført en primærpsykiatrisk undersøkelse av siktede og innhentet rapporter, ifølge politiet.
Det var ikke Høiby som anmeldte saken.
– Det var politiet som opprettet saken, og det har ingen betydning for oss at dette blir henlagt. Det viktigste for oss er at hans sikkerhet er ivaretatt, noe Høiby opplever at den er, sier Høibys forsvarer Alexander Greaker i en uttalelse til VG.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Utbrudd av influensa: – Ta vaksinen nå</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/utbrudd-av-influensa_-_-ta-vaksinen-na-1.18089136</link>
      <description>Vinterens influensautbrudd er i gang. Samtidig øker koronasmitten.
Det opplyser Folkehelseinstituttet torsdag.
– Beskyttelse mot influensa og covid-19 oppnås én til to uker etter at du har tatt vaksine. Det er derfor viktig at de som er anbefalt vaksine tar den nå, før smitten øker ytterligere, sier overlege Ingvild Fjeldheim ved FHI.
Vaksine er det viktigste tiltaket for å beskytte risikogrupper og eldre mot alvorlig influensa- og koronasykdom, heter det.
Men forsinkelser i leveransene har ført til at enkelte kommuner har måttet vente med vaksineringen. Dette problemet skal imidlertid være løst nå.
– Har du måtte utsette vaksineringen fordi vaksinen ikke var tilgjengelig, oppfordrer vi deg til å ta vaksine nå, sier Fjeldheim.
Disse anbefales å ta influensavaksinen:
• Alle fra fylte 65 år.
• Barn og voksne i definerte risikogrupper.
• Gravide etter 12. svangerskapsuke, og tidligere i svangerskapet ved tilleggsrisiko.
• Helsepersonell med nær pasientkontakt.</description>
      <category>Influensa</category>
      <pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:14:16 GMT</pubDate>

      <title>Nusa-dobbel for Leipzig i Meisterligaen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nusa-dobbel-for-leipzig-i-meisterligaen-1.18088054</link>
      <description>Antonio Nusa briljerte med heile to scoringar for RB Leipzig i kampen mot franske Lens.
Nusa markerte seg allereie frå start og sørga for det andre av to mål for Leipzig i første omgang før det var gått ti minutt.
Etter pausen var franskmennene litt meir på ballen og fekk utteljing då Matthieu Udol plukka opp ein retur etter eit blokkert skot og sette ballen i mål.
Mot slutten sette Leipzig alle mann i angrep og Nusa fekk ein enkel jobb med å setta si andre scoring, få sekund før dommaren blåste av kampen.
Stillinga blei til slutt 3–1 til tyskarane, medan Lens held fram med skuffande resultat.
Den franske klubben vann den første kampen i Meisterligaen i haust, men har sidan gått på fire strake tap.
9. desember møter dei Bodø/Glimt på heimebane.
Martin Ødegaard og Arsenal spelte uavgjort mot Borussia Dortmund og Julian Ryerson.
Det same gjorde Manchester City som klarte å utlikna til 2–2 mot Napoli i det 86. speleminuttet, sjølv om Erling Braut Haaland var mållaus gjennom heile kampen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Skandalen i Afrikamesterskapet: Senegal får tilbake tittelen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>

      <description>Etter at de rødgrønne partiene ikke klarte å lykkes i å lande en avtale om neste års statsbudsjett søndag kveld, må de fortsette forhandlingene mandag.

    <item>
      <title>Danmark: 120 avviste asylsøkere kan sendes til Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/danmark_-120-avviste-asylsokere-kan-sendes-til-rwanda-1.18086852</link>
      <description>120 avviste asylsøkere i Danmark oppfyller kriteriene for å bli sendt til et retursenter i Rwanda neste år.
Det opplyser det danske utlendings- og integreringsdepartementet til DR.
Det er bare asylsøkere som ikke har barn eller er blitt dømt til kriminalitet som kan bli sendt til Rwanda, ifølge allmennkringkasteren. Dette skal gjelde 120 av 365 avviste asylsøkere.
Danmark er ett av fem EU-land som er enige om å etablere et felles retursenter for asylsøkere i Rwanda.</description>

      <description>En person ble fraktet til sykehus etter en voldshendelse i Førde søndag, opplyser Vest politidistrikt.

Mel Lingerie has been a downtown Victoria staple for six years, and now the owner is taking her experience to politics.

Melissa Cseszko opened Mel Lingerie in 2020, which offers more than your regular bra shopping experience.

Each customer is greeted and given a glass of bubbly or a cup of tea.

“Some people have just had horrible experiences,” Cseszko said.

“This just takes a little bit of the edge off to make them feel more comfortable.”

Guests are pampered, encouraged, and made to feel special doing something many women detest.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“It’s the most fulfilling retail I’ve ever worked,” says Emily Finch.

“We’ve had women coming in, and they’re like ‘I hate bra shopping, I never find my size, I never find anything that works.’ Then I get to be the little, like, bra fairy, the little angel on their shoulder that goes, ‘No it’s not you, it’s the bra.'”

The reason for opening the store comes from a personal place.

“She opened the store because she got ghosted like two weeks before her wedding,” Finch said. “So she is just so understanding.”

The products in the store are diligently sourced, often from women-owned companies who are responsible in their production practices, materials, and the way employees are treated.

At Mel Lingerie, the employees are treated like family.

“She’s a very safe person to talk to and open up to in that way, and I think that’s part of the reason so many people feel so safe,” Finch said.

And now, Cseszko is taking her experience to a new office, just 550 metres away from her Fort Street store.

“Right now, people can’t really afford to be down here. Not only to live, to park, to come,” Cseszko said.

James Booker shuffled through downtown Nanaimo Friday, looking for shelter, with a cough and cold that he said is getting worse by the day. The unhoused man endured this week’s back to back storms, living in Nanaimo doorways and under tarps, because there weren’t enough shelter beds to meet the demand. 

“It was horrible. I had pneumonia three times this year, and its exactly that kind of thing that triggers the pneumonia to come back…That’s just the first of many winter storms, and its not even winter yet,” said Booker.

Marnie Boers is a newly-elected City of Nanaimo Councillor, and an Emergency Room nurse. Boers said the critical shortage of shelter beds is a health issue here, especially since extreme weather response shelters didn’t open during the recent storms, because the weather didn’t meet the cold threshold needed to access funding from BC Housing.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“Right now we have 163 shelter beds within community. But that really only represents 16 per cent, if you compare that to how many people are outside. So in other communities, Victoria, Vancouver, they have 60 to 70 per cent. In Nanaimo, we are significantly underserved,” said Boers.

Adam Wright has lived in Nanaimo for 30 years, and says he is seeing more homeless people on the streets now than ever.

“You didn’t see any of this. All of the heavy drugs, they did it indoors, they hid. Now all their facilities have been taken away and they’re all on the street,” Wright told CHEK News.

Boers says the increasing frequency of extreme weather events, delivering days of heavy rains and high winds, instead of snow and cold temperatures, prompted her and other Nanaimo city councillors to call for the province to change its threshold for extreme weather. That move could trigger more shelter beds to open in storms like the ones that hit the south coast this week.

“Because in this last storm, we didn’t have any avenues to open anything up. Even though we all heard how torrential the rain was, and miserable it was to be outside for even five minutes. We just don’t have a pathway that could be activated. We need to be able to prepare ourselves for more precipitation and heavy winds,” said Boers.

Nanaimo’s homeless weren’t alone, facing the storms outside. Cowichan’s Temporary Winter Shelter that is slated for the math annex of the old Cowichan Secondary School wasn’t opened in time for this week’s storms either. The Cowichan Valley Regional District board says it is still waiting for needed funding from BC Housing to open it.

Fortunately, so far the weather forecast is offering a break between storms, for that needed funding to start flowing to the communities relying on it.

The benches along the oceanside stretch of Dallas Road in Victoria provide more than just a scenic rest stop, they are the focus of a professor’s unique research project at Royal Roads University.

Victoria resident Paul Brault sits on his two favourite benches every day during his daily walks.

“I really like them. and i use them all the time. And now that they’ve put in the new benches, it’s actually better. It looks nice.”

Along this five-kilometre stretch of Dallas Road, from James Bay to Ross Bay, there are 214 benches. These fixtures are now the centre of academic attention from Royal Roads University professor Phillip Vannini.

“The benches have stories, and they have heard countless conversations like this. I can’t ask a bench about all the stories that it has heard. But I can ask the people about the time that they have spent here. through those stories I can weave a much bigger story about life on Vancouver Island,” Vannini said.

For the next two years, Vannini is collecting stories for a research project, and a documentary called Dallas Road Stories. From Fisherman’s Wharf to the start of Hollywood Crescent he’s going to collect stories from each of the benches told by the people who use them.

He says the benches, are part of what make Dallas Road unique.

“I can’t think of a place, I’ve been to fifty countries around the world, I can’t think of a city street that is so close to downtown where you have so much wildlife, and where you have so much. People take time here, and it’s a rare resource. It’s a bit of a rare find,” Vannini said.

Just weeks into his research, what has surprised him the most are the items people leave for others on the benches. A scarf left behind on a cold day. Or a wind phone located in a quiet spot at Clover Point so people can symbolically talk to someone they have lost.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“It’s just one example of the things people leave on benches for others to take time with. And you don’t really see that anywhere else,’ Vannini said.

There are no playgrounds along Dallas Road, and the last chance to spend money is Ogden Point. The focus is the beauty, the quiet, and a chance to sit and enjoy it.
And the benches are weaved into daily lives.

Brault points to the bench behind him, and remarks that it’s often decorated.

“I’ve noticed that a lot; like this one over here, people decorate it at Christmas time. Or there was a memorial on there a week ago, a month ago,” Brault said.

Vannini said this stretch of city is so important because it’s part of daily life.

“It’s here. And by this I mean there’s beauty in local. This is our city’s backyard or front deck. And it’s a place where everyone remembers,” Vannini said.

And Vannini would like to hear more Dallas Road Stories.
He can be reached via email at: dallasroadstories@gmail.com.

Evacuation alerts have also been cancelled for the following properties on Headquarters Road (Maple Pool/Headquarters): 4697, 4685, 4679, 4673, 4667, 4661, 4659, 4653, and 4629.

“Residents are now returning home, with most having already returned,” states the Comox Valley EOC.

It adds that community assessments are also continuing to inform the district of the full extent of the flooding impacts.

Among those evacuated, Emergency Support Services (ESS) supported 97 evacuated residents. ESS is now moving to case management work, and this reception centre is no longer active.

CVRD Board Chair Arzeena Hamir says there’s still significant work ahead in the recovery process.

“Flooding has affected residents and communities across the region, and we recognize that the work doesn’t end when the immediate emergency is over.”

“Our ongoing collaboration is essential to supporting people in the Comox Valley as we transition from response to recovery,” said Hamir.

The kits include a mop, sponges, brooms, gloves, and other supplies to safely clean flood-affected homes and properties.

As the recovery work begins, local K’ómoks First Nation Chief Nicole Rempel is reminding residents to take care of themselves and each other.

BC Hydro is continuing to release water from the reservoir to help manage the water levels. Though conditions are improving, the EOC reminds residents to remain vigilant as weather conditions can change quickly.

Residents are asked to “avoid rivers, waterways, and low-lying areas, where water levels and conditions can change rapidly.”

It’s a campaign promise Saanich’s newly elected mayor and slate of councillors ran on: a pause on building bike lanes.

Come Monday, council will consider a motion asking for just that.

“Maybe there’s better alternatives. So at this point we just want to pause, regroup and see what we can do to accommodate everybody. We want to create a safe environment for both cyclists and drivers and pedestrians and everybody else,” said Matt McGeachie, Saanich councillor.

“We’re getting so much backlash, like, oh my god, we’re going back to the neanderthal days. And that’s really not what it is, we want to sit and review,” he said.

Coun. Lorne DeLarge is proposing a motion to place an “immediate moratorium on the installation of any further bicycle lanes and traffic calming initiatives.”

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“This moratorium shall not apply where a legally binding contract is already in place prior to the adoption of this resolution, or halting or cancelling work would result in financial, legal, or operational harm to the district, or failing to proceed with installation of or signage would create an immediate public safety concern,” the motion reads.

Cycling advocacy group Capital Bike is concerned that Saanich’s new council is reversing course on road safety.

“I think I would just ask council to engage with subject matter expertise on this, not just going with vibes and the feelings of angry people who get stuck in traffic,” said Colleen Sparks, chair of Capital Bike’s Saanich committee.

UVic public policy professor Katya Rhodes says she’s “disappointed” by the motion.

“I was upset and disappointed and actually confused about why we would want that,” she said.

Rhodes and her colleague Sarah Wiebe are worried that this signals a backwards policy slide on road safety.

They argue that when it comes to factoring in affordability, health or climate change, more bike lanes should be built.

“It seems like there’s maybe a concern that with bike lines there’s more congestion, more traffic, which simply isn’t the case. The more infrastructure we have the less cars there will be on the road,” said Wiebe, also a UVic public policy professor.

“My take is that the frustrations that some residents have expressed are based in the fact there has been poor consultation,” said Rhodes. “So the problem is the public engagement process. There are easy fixes to that.”

The lack of consultation seems to surround Mann Avenue, a stretch of road between Wilkinson Road and Glanford Avenue.

McGeachie says streetside parking was eliminated and bike lanes were installed without proper consultation.

“One day parking was there, and then it was gone,” said McGeachie. “I’ve heard from cyclists that live on Mann Avenue that don’t like it…I think the vast majority of them don’t like it, and the lack of parking is a big thing for them.”

“It’s just a conversation. That’s really what I want, is a conversation about how we can fix this so everyone is happy,” he said.

McGeachie wants to look at alternatives for the Mann Avenue bike lane, like Centennial Trail, which runs parallel to Mann Road.

“I don’t know if it was even explored,” said McGeachie.

The Mann Avenue bike lanes were installed over summer 2026. Saanich held two rounds of public engagement on the project.

Saanich council will debate the motions Monday, Nov. 30.

]]> 1364984 Union Bay shipbreaking facility trial postponed to February https://cheknews.ca/union-bay-shipbreaking-facility-trial-postponed-to-february-1365063/ Fri, 27 Nov 2026 23:33:11 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1365063

Union Bay will have to wait a few more months for answers on the ongoing shipbreaking facility saga after the trial dates were postponed to February.

The Comox Valley Regional District was supposed to have its case heard against Union Bay Industries and Deep Water Recovery from Nov. 25-27, but on Wednesday the dates were postponed due to a lack of an available judge.

It will now instead be heard Feb. 3, 4 and 5, 2027.

The trial will hear whether or not Deep Water Recovery is doing business on the land that is permitted in the current zoning.

The CVRD argues that the land is not zoned to permit shipbreaking.

“The Ship Breaking Use is not a permitted use of the Property under the Zoning Bylaw, and is prohibited by the Zoning Bylaw,” the CVRD’s claim says.

The CVRD is seeking a declaration that the ship breaking and housing use are in contravention of its zoning bylaw, an order that the companies must cease and desist the ship breaking, and that the housing use must cease and desist as well, in addition to other relief.

Union Bay Industries owns the land and leases it to Deep Water Recovery. The two deny the allegations that shipbreaking is not a permitted use.

“Deep Water has, on occasion, been tasked with performing emergency rescue services on behalf of the Canadian government and the Canadian Coast Guard,” the response to the civil claim says.

“To date, Deep Water’s activities have never included work on any motorized vessels, with the exception of one small wooden vessel delivered by the Canadian Coast Guard, as referenced above.”

The response also claims that the CVRD “previously approved Deep Water’s operations, and, on its own admission, considered those operations to be compliant with the Zoning Bylaw,” the response says.

“However, after sustained lobbying by local residents and organized community groups, the Plaintiff succumbed to external pressure and saw Deep Water’s operations as politically unpopular.”

Former British Columbia environment minister and labour leader George Heyman has died, the province’s main public employee union says.

The BC General Employees’ Union says in a release that Heyman died Friday morning, but it did not provide a cause of death.

Heyman had a lengthy and decorated career in B.C.’s labour movement, acting as the president of the BCGEU for three terms starting in 1999.

The union says he was among the first labour leaders in B.C. to link climate action to the labour movement, eventually leaving the BCGEU in 2008 and becoming executive director of Sierra Club BC before entering politics in 2013.

He was elected as an MLA in Vancouver-Fairview that year and re-elected again in 2017 and 2020, and served as B.C.’s environment minister from 2017 to 2024.

In a statement posted on social media, B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson says he is “terribly saddened” by Heyman’s death, saying the former New Democrat MLA had “devoted much of his life to public service and to the causes he believed in.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 27, 2026.
